description: Two-panel figure of X-ray diffraction traces (y-axis: Intensity (A.U.); x-axis: Position (2 Theta) in degrees, labelled ticks 30-90 with data spanning roughly 20-100°), acquired with Cu-Kα radiation on Fe-7 wt.% Al alloys of different carbon content. (a) Fe-7 wt.% Al-0.012 wt.% C: intensity ticks 0, 100, 200; the dominant (220)Fe3Al reflection sits just past the 40° gridline and rises above the 200 line, with weaker (111)Fe3Al, (400)Fe3Al, (422)Fe3Al and (440)Fe3Al reflections distributed from before 30° to near the right-hand edge. (b) Fe-7 wt.% Al-0.15 wt.% C: intensity ticks 0, 50, 100; the same (220)Fe3Al peak again dominates (above the 100 line) and the Fe3Al (111), (400), (422) and (440) reflections reappear, but two additional reflections are labelled — (200)Fe3AlC0.5 adjacent to the main peak near 44° and (311)Fe3AlC0.5 near 84°. The extra Fe3AlC0.5 (κ-carbide) reflections present only in the higher-carbon alloy demonstrate that carbon addition precipitates Fe3AlC0.5, which the citing text confirms by XRD and reports increasing in volume fraction with carbon content.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an XRD trace whose tallest reflection is labelled (220)Fe3Al and lies just past the 40° 2θ gridline, rising above the 200 A.U. intensity gridline.
Panel (a) labels only Fe3Al reflections: (111)Fe3Al, (220)Fe3Al, (400)Fe3Al, (422)Fe3Al and (440)Fe3Al; no carbide peaks are indexed.
Panel (b) shows the same Fe3Al reflection set plus two additional labelled reflections, (200)Fe3AlC0.5 (adjacent to the main peak near 44° 2θ) and (311)Fe3AlC0.5 (near 84° 2θ).
Both panels plot Intensity (A.U.) against Position (2 Theta); panel (a) intensity axis is labelled 0, 100, 200 and panel (b) 0, 50, 100, with 2θ gridline ticks at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80 and 90.
Exact 2θ positions of the peaks are not printed numerically; they can only be read relative to the axis gridlines.
The caption states the traces were recorded using Cu-Kα radiation.
The caption identifies panel (a) as Fe-7 wt.% Al-0.012 wt.% C and panel (b) as Fe-7 wt.% Al-0.15 wt.% C.
The caption states that similar Fe3Al and Fe3AlC0.5 peaks were observed in three other alloys with carbon 0.35-1 wt.%.
The citing text states the precipitates were confirmed to be Fe3AlC0.5 by X-ray diffraction analysis using a Philips 3710 x-ray diffractometer.
The citing text states that the volume fraction of these precipitates increases significantly with increasing carbon content.

The citing text states that the alloy with 0.02 C showed a single-phase structure with no precipitates, in contrast to higher-carbon alloys which contained significant precipitate amounts; this carbon value (0.02) differs from the 0.012 wt.% C printed in the caption for panel (a).
The figure establishes that Fe3AlC0.5 (κ-carbide) reflections appear in the 2θ range shown only for the higher-carbon alloy (b), making the presence of Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates carbon-dependent.

subfigures.description: XRD trace (Intensity (A.U.) vs Position (2 Theta), ticks 0/100/200) for Fe-7 wt.% Al-0.012 wt.% C. Only Fe3Al reflections are labelled: (111)Fe3Al just before 30°, a dominant (220)Fe3Al just past 40° rising above the 200 a.u. line, (400)Fe3Al between 60 and 70°, (422)Fe3Al between 80 and 90°, and a weak (440)Fe3Al at the far right edge near 100°.

XRD trace (Intensity (A.U.) vs Position (2 Theta), ticks 0/50/100) for Fe-7 wt.% Al-0.15 wt.% C. Fe3Al (111), (220), (400), (422) and (440) reflections reappear, with the (220)Fe3Al peak above the 100 a.u. line, plus two extra labelled reflections of Fe3AlC0.5: (200)Fe3AlC0.5 next to the main peak near 44° and (311)Fe3AlC0.5 near 84°.
